daily_actions.action: Pull latest webrobots.io monthly Kickstarter dump, filter locally for state=successful, category in [Tabletop Games, Hardware, Design], pledged>=$100K, deadline 60-120 days ago -> shortlist CSV
Run Apify xtracto/kickstarter-projects discover-mode actor on target categories with enrichment on; compute distress_score = comments_count / updates_count and days_since_deadline
Skim BackerLens sourcing-ready list, Indiegogo InDemand explore page, and BoardGameGeek fulfillment threads for qualitative distress signals a script can't judge (tone, named creators melting down)
Merge Kickstarter + Indiegogo + Shopify (StoreLeads) rows into one ~200-row prospect sheet; spot-check 20 random rows for sanity before outreach starts
Run Hunter.io domain search + Apify Kickstarter Email Scraper against that day's shortlist to attach and verify contact emails
Manually open the day's top 10 highest-distress-score campaigns, read latest 3 updates + comment section, tag genuine hard-late vs just-slow
Weekly: pull StoreLeads export for PreProduct/Purple Dot install lists, dedupe against existing CRM/prospect sheet
Approve or reject that day's outreach batch before any message sends

items.name: webrobots.io monthly Kickstarter dataset
items.what: Free full monthly re-scrape of every Kickstarter project (live + ended), JSON/CSV, running since 2014-2016 to present.
items.how: Go to webrobots.io/kickstarter-datasets/, download the latest month's CSV.zip (~30 files, ~100MB), concat locally, filter for state=successful AND category in [Tabletop Games, Hardware, Design/Product Design] AND pledged>=$100K AND deadline 60-120 days ago. No scraping required, it's a pre-built export.
items.risk: Third-party recompiled Kickstarter data; Kickstarter's ToS forbids bulk harvesting but webrobots.io has run openly since 2014 without apparent takedown. Use only for lead gen, never republish/resell the raw dataset.

items.name: Apify: xtracto/kickstarter-projects (Discover mode)
items.what: Paid Kickstarter scraper actor mirroring KS's own discover filters (categoryIds, state, sort), with optional enrichment returning updates_count/comments_count/rewards - your best programmatic proxy for 'funded and going quiet while backers get loud.'
items.how: Run via Apify console with categoryIds=[Tabletop Games, Hardware, Design], state=successful, sort=end_date, maxItems=500-1000, enrichment=true; export CSV; compute distress_score = comments_count / max(updates_count,1).
items.cost: $20.00 per 1,000 results, pay-per-event, plus Apify platform usage (Free plan = $5/mo credit, Starter = $29/mo)
items.risk: Scraping Kickstarter has no official sanction and violates KS's ToS on bulk harvesting; Apify's proxy handling makes it harder to block, not compliant. Keep volume modest (hundreds/week), use for lead gen only.

items.name: BackerLens (sourcing-ready)
items.what: Free purpose-built directory of campaigns already in Indiegogo InDemand or Kickstarter Late Pledge - i.e. funded and still actively selling post-deadline. Shows funding total, % funded, category, 24h momentum, and a proprietary 'LENS' score. ~1,473 campaigns tracked (1,431 Indiegogo / 42 Kickstarter) as of this check.
items.how: Create a free account at backerlens.com/sourcing-ready, filter by category/funding range, list campaign names+links, then open each to check delivery-date-vs-today gap and comment tone.
items.risk: low - first-party public directory, no scraping involved

items.name: StoreLeads
items.what: Ecommerce store intelligence DB covering 2.9M Shopify stores with installed-app + install-date data; filter for stores running preorder/deposit apps (PreProduct, Purple Dot, Notify Me!, PreOrder Globo) as a proxy for brands currently selling on a wait.
items.how: Sign up Premium to browse/filter by app=PreProduct OR Purple Dot; upgrade to Pro only the month you need bulk CSV/API export, then downgrade. Cross-reference the resulting stores against Shopify's public estimated-revenue field to prioritize mid-size brands.

items.name: Indiegogo InDemand direct browse
items.what: Indiegogo's own ongoing marketplace of funded campaigns still accepting late pledges - every campaign here is, by definition, still fulfilling.
items.how: Browse indiegogo.com/explore and BackerLens's larger Indiegogo-side pool (1,431 campaigns) side by side; sort by category/funding size, open each to check latest update date vs today.
items.risk: low, manual browsing of public pages

items.name: Kicktraq
items.what: Long-running (since 2012) third-party Kickstarter analytics/discovery site plus browser extension; Hot List and per-project pledge-history graphs let you visually spot campaigns that spiked then went quiet - a fulfillment-risk tell.
items.how: Browse kicktraq.com/projects (Active Projects) and the Hot List; install the free Chrome extension so pledge-history overlays show while browsing Kickstarter itself.

items.name: Kickstarter Advanced Search / Discover (native)
items.what: Kickstarter's own filter UI - project state, category/subcategory, amount-pledged ranges, sort by end date - the fastest zero-cost way to hand-pick campaigns that ended 60-120 days ago in target categories.
items.how: Use kickstarter.com/discover/advanced with state=successful, category=Tabletop Games or Design/Technology, sort=end_date; open results manually. Direct bot/script fetches to this page return 403, so this lane is human browsing (Dylan, or a real browser session), not a script target.
items.risk: low for manual browsing; confirmed Kickstarter blocks non-browser automated fetches (403), don't try to script it directly

items.name: BoardGameGeek fulfillment threads
items.what: Tabletop backers self-organize public 'Kickstarter Update' and shipping-delay threads per game, naming the exact publisher and describing exactly how late/how angry - highest-signal, zero-tooling qualitative source for 'who is melting down right now' in tabletop.
items.how: Search boardgamegeek.com for '[category] kickstarter delay' or browse the community delay-analysis threads and their comments for named campaigns; also check a specific game's own forum for 'fulfillment update' threads.

items.name: Gamefound (search page + public API)
items.what: Dominant tabletop-crowdfunding platform after Kickstarter; official public API exposes creator lookup and active-project listing but has no category/funding filter, so pair it with manual search-page browsing.
items.how: Browse gamefound.com/en/projects/search manually for funded, past-deadline tabletop campaigns; use the public API to pull creator metadata once you have a shortlist of URL slugs.

items.name: Apify: Kickstarter Email Scraper (contactminerlabs)
items.what: Actor that searches Kickstarter by keyword and extracts publicly-listed emails + creator/project links tied to the search - cheapest at-scale contact-discovery tool in this stack.
items.how: Run with KEYWORD=target category term, MAX_ITEMS=200-500, optional DOMAIN_EMAIL filter to strip @kickstarter.com noise. Treat output as unverified - run every email through a verifier before sending.
items.risk: Coverage/accuracy unverified (third-party actor). Scraping public emails for cold outreach still needs CAN-SPAM/GDPR-compliant sending (real sender ID, unsubscribe). Mitigate: verify before send, keep daily volume small.

items.name: Hunter.io domain search
items.what: Once you have a creator's own website (usually linked from their KS bio or campaign story), Hunter finds/verifies the best contact email on that domain.
items.how: Paste the creator's domain into Hunter's Domain Search; 1 credit per email found.
items.cost: free (50 credits/mo) or $34/mo Starter for more volume

items.name: Preorder-vendor client/case-study pages (Purple Dot, PreProduct)
items.what: Purple Dot and PreProduct specifically serve pay-later/long-lead-time preorders (closer to Tideover's actual ICP than generic restock-notify apps like Notify Me!). Their own marketing sites list named enterprise clients and case studies - a small, free, pre-qualified, higher-ACV shortlist that StoreLeads structurally under-detects because these vendors use custom/enterprise integrations.
items.how: Visit getpurpledot.com and preproduct.io, pull every named customer/case-study logo, cross-check each brand's live Shopify store for a 'ships in X weeks' preorder banner.

items.name: ScrapingBee Kickstarter Scraper API
items.what: On-demand single-page scraper (handles proxy rotation/bot-detection) returning full campaign+creator detail for one URL at a time - not built for bulk discovery, but useful to enrich a final shortlist right before outreach.
items.how: Call the API per-URL for your top 30-50 shortlisted campaigns to pull creator profile fields/bio links that bulk-discovery actors miss.
items.cost: 1,000 free credits to start, then $49/mo (250K credits) up to $599/mo (8M credits); JS-rendered request = 5 credits
items.risk: low, but too expensive per-record for bulk work - reserve for shortlist enrichment only

items.name: Apollo.io / Snov.io (backup contact enrichment)
items.what: Sales-intelligence databases for finding a named creator's business email/LinkedIn once you know their name and company - backup/cross-check to Hunter when a domain search comes up empty.
items.how: Search by creator name + company; use as a spot-check, not primary volume, given thin free tiers.
items.cost: free (Apollo 100 credits/mo since late-2025 restructure, or Snov 50 credits/mo), paid from $39/mo (Snov, 1,000 credits) or $49/user/mo (Apollo Basic, 1,000 credits)

load_bearing_claims.claim: Kickstarter has no official public API and its Terms of Service explicitly forbid bulk harvesting/scraping ('access or copy in bulk, retrieve, harvest, or index any portion of the Services'); the platform also actively blocks automated bots.
webrobots.io publishes a free full monthly re-scrape of all Kickstarter projects in JSON/CSV, run continuously on a monthly cadence since March 2016.

The Apify actor xtracto/kickstarter-projects charges $20.00 per 1,000 results and supports a Discover mode filtering by categoryIds/state/sort with optional enrichment returning updates_count and comments_count.
StoreLeads tracks installed-app data across 2.9M Shopify stores; Premium tier is $75/mo (browse only), CSV/API export requires the $250/mo Pro tier.
Hunter.io's free plan in 2026 provides 50 credits/month (roughly 50 email finds), with paid plans starting at $34/mo (Starter).

A 534,514-store Shopify scan found Notify Me! on 3,535 stores, PreOrder Globo on 2,391, PreProduct on 132, and Purple Dot on 65 - with the study noting Purple Dot's enterprise/custom-integration clients are likely undercounted by public detection.

summary: Fastest path to a 200-row prospect list: pull webrobots.io's free monthly Kickstarter dump and BackerLens's free curated late-pledge/InDemand list first (zero cost, same day), then layer in Apify's $20/1,000-result Kickstarter discover actor and StoreLeads ($75-250/mo) for Shopify preorder-app install data to hit volume. Kickstarter has no official API, actively blocks bot traffic (confirmed 403 on direct automated fetch), and its ToS forbids bulk harvesting - treat any Kickstarter-side scraping (Apify, ScrapingBee) as tolerated-but-not-sanctioned, keep volumes modest, and never republish the raw data. "Distressed and in fulfillment" is best detected by combining machine signals (deadline 60-120 days past, updates_count low relative to age, comments_count high) from Apify's enrichment fields with human spot-checks of BoardGameGeek threads and campaign comment walls, which name specific angry creators directly and for free. For contact discovery, Kickstarter's own in-platform creator inbox (free) plus Hunter.io domain search (free 50/mo) covers most volume cheaply; the $9.99/mo Apify email scraper is the highest-leverage paid add but needs verification before sending. On the Shopify side, target PreProduct's and Purple Dot's install base specifically over generic restock apps like Notify Me! - they serve genuine pay-later/long-wait preorders, a tighter ICP match, and their own case-study pages are a free pre-qualified shortlist that StoreLeads structurally undercounts.
